hypothesis: Selecting distinct provider-symbol mechanisms for long and short exposure may produce a stronger bidirectional shared-capital portfolio than requiring every provider route to work symmetrically on both sides.
decision: Adopt the separate-side composition report as a report-only research baseline, keep the armed v25 runtime unchanged, and do not revive retired v29. The current frontier is not ready to define a successor portfolio: HYPE HT-Breakout long is the only component with repeated positive mixed-profile live history, its eight closes conflict with adverse historical route-shape evidence, and no short component has repeated positive live evidence. Across all mixed-profile history, 22 long closes net +$2.250476 while 11 short closes net -$2.128212, leaving only +$0.122264 overall; one single-trade SOL long contributes +$1.582877, so the pooled result is outlier-dependent. Preserve all long and short candidates in the research ledger, but require a new-generation interaction experiment to keep current-profile outcomes, mixed-profile outcomes, execution costs, and shared-capital overlap separate before any future explicit authorization decision.
falsifier: This decision is invalidated by evidence hash or scope drift, side-identity collisions, pooling current-profile and mixed-profile outcomes, omission of fees or funding from claimed net results, or any report-only code changing runtime state. The weak-short conclusion would update after repeated independent after-friction short lifecycles. The HYPE-long priority would weaken if additional compatible closes make its net PnL or median return on margin nonpositive, or if shared-capital replay shows adverse overlap dominates its standalone contribution.
limitations: All-live history spans multiple profile generations and therefore cannot establish current-v25 route edge.
The only repeated-positive component, HYPE HT-Breakout long, has no compatible current-v25 close and conflicts with adverse historical route-shape evidence.
The short frontier contains one single-trade positive mixed-profile observation and one historically supportive route with zero compatible live closes.
The largest positive mixed-profile component is a single SOL long whose +$1.582877 exceeds the +$0.122264 total mixed-profile net, so aggregate profitability is highly outlier-dependent.
Every resolved current-v25 close at this cutoff is long; current-profile short-side economics remain unobserved.
Standalone component rankings do not model simultaneous signals, slot contention, correlated exposure, leverage utilization, or shared-capital path dependence.
The ranking does not estimate an allocator, risk contribution, turnover, break-even cost, or portfolio drawdown distribution.
A positive net field is accepted only within the source audit's stated fee and funding scope; hidden liquidity, queue position, latency, and opportunity cost remain unmodeled.
The descriptive threshold of five closes is a reporting convention, not a statistical significance or promotion gate.
No live route, position, order, stop, target, size, exit, transition drain, or protection changed in this revision.
